communityBenefit.source: Memorial Hermann FY2024 Community Report ($472M); FY2025 report claims $530M+; 66% of community benefit is unreimbursed care costs; Texas Health & Safety Code Section 311.045 requires nonprofit hospitals to provide community benefit of at least 5% of net patient revenue with at least 4% in charity care; Lown Institute found 42% of Texas private nonprofit hospitals had fair-share deficits (2020-2022)

taxAdvantage.notes: Memorial Hermann operates 17 hospitals and numerous clinics across Harris, Fort Bend, Montgomery and surrounding counties, all property-tax-exempt. Texas has no state income tax. Federal income tax foregone on $860M net income (FY2024) would be substantial. Tax-exempt bond interest subsidy applies to $1.1B+ in outstanding debt.

ratios.investmentsToOperatingIncomeInterpretati: Operating income not separately verifiable from 990 total excess revenue; investment portfolio of ~$4.95B (Form 990 Part X Lines 11-13, FY2024 end-of-year) generated $408M in investment income at an approximate 8.2% return; if total excess revenue of ~$860M is used as proxy for operating income, ratio would be approximately 5.8x
ratios.bondDebtToCommunityBenefitInterpretation: Memorial Hermann carries $2.33 in tax-exempt bond debt for every $1 it claims in community benefit ($1.1B debt vs $472M claimed community benefit)
ratios.charityCareVsStateInterpretation: Memorial Hermann claims 5.5% of revenue in community benefit, just above the Texas statutory minimum of 5%; 66% of that total is unreimbursed care costs rather than direct charity care; Lown Institute found 42% of Texas private nonprofit hospitals had fair-share deficits

accusation: Holds $9.1 billion in net assets and $13.7 billion in total assets, generated $408 million in investment income in a single year, yet claims only 5.5% of revenue in community benefit — barely exceeding Texas's 5% statutory floor — while closing its nursing and senior living facilities, winding down its commercial health plan, and offering buyouts to nonclinical workers under a 'strategic acceleration plan' citing financial pressures.
